bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Head Teacher Salary in NSW

If you are a head teacher in New South Wales, you may be offered an hourly rate or a salary package. Converting between the two helps you compare offers and plan your budget. This guide explains the standard calculation, how tax and super work, and where award rates fit in.

### The Basic Conversion Formula

The annual salary from an hourly rate is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

We assume a standard full-time week of 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Act. So the total working hours per year are 38 × 52 = 1,976 hours.

For example, if your hourly rate is $50, your annual salary is $50 × 1,976 = $98,800. This is your gross pay before tax and super.

If you are paid fortnightly, your gross fortnightly pay is your weekly pay multiplied by 2. Using the same example, weekly pay is $50 × 38 = $1,900, so fortnightly pay is $3,800.

### What About the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates?

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. However, head teachers are covered by the Teachers Award, which sets higher minimum rates based on classification and experience. The award rate for a head teacher is likely above the National Minimum Wage, so always check your specific award or enterprise agreement.

If you are a casual head teacher, your hourly rate should already include the 25% casual loading. When using our [the timesheet](/) calculator, do not add casual loading on top of a rate that already includes it. The calculator has a checkbox to add 25% loading if needed.

### How Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. For a $98,800 annual salary, the super contribution would be $11,856 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit.

### Estimating Tax and Take-Home Pay

For the 2026–27 financial year, the Australian resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- Over $190,000: 45%

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here).

For a $98,800 annual salary, tax would be approximately $20,467 plus Medicare levy of $1,976, giving total deductions of $22,443. Your take-home pay would be about $76,357 per year, or $6,363 per month. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a more detailed estimate.

### Comparing with NSW Average Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult ordinary time earnings in New South Wales were $2,108.80 per week in May 2026. This is an average across all occupations and industries, not a median for head teachers. Your head teacher salary may differ based on your school, experience, and enterprise agreement.

### Key Points to Remember

- Annual pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52. This assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.
- Super is 12% on top, up to the maximum contribution base.
- Tax is estimated using the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold.
- Casual loading (25%) is added on top of the base rate if applicable.
- Always check your award or agreement for your correct minimum rate. Our [pay guides](/blog) can help you find the right classification.

Understanding your head teacher salary in NSW starts with knowing your hourly rate and the standard conversion.
